title: Decision 44 COM 7A.34: Deletion of 'Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City' from the World Heritage List (2021)
body: UNESCO World Heritage Committee (extended 44th session, 2021; this is a decision of the World Heritage Committee, not a court or UN Security Council action)
case_reference: Decision 44 COM 7A.34 (working document WHC/21/44.COM/7A.Add); related Decision 44 COM 8C.4
summary: On 21 July 2021, at its extended 44th session, the UNESCO World Heritage Committee decided in Decision 44 COM 7A.34 to delete 'Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City' (United Kingdom) from the World Heritage List. UNESCO's news release gives the reason as 'irreversible loss of attributes conveying the outstanding universal value', and states that the property had been inscribed in 2004 and placed on the List of World Heritage in Danger in 2012 over the proposed Liverpool Waters development, and that Liverpool is the third property to lose World Heritage status, after the Elbe Valley in Dresden (Germany) and the Arabian Oryx Sanctuary (Oman). The decision regrets that inadequate governance of new developments caused serious and irreversible loss, names the Liverpool Waters project and other large works, and says an approved stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock adds to the threat.
legal_basis: The decision is taken by the World Heritage Committee under the 1972 World Heritage Convention. Article 11(4) of the Convention provides for a List of World Heritage in Danger for properties threatened by 'serious and specific dangers', which the Article lists as including 'large-scale public or private projects', 'rapid urban or tourist development projects' and 'the outbreak or the threat of an armed conflict'; Article 11(4) also lets the Committee make a new entry 'at any time, in case of urgent need'. Article 4 says the duty of identifying, protecting, conserving, presenting and transmitting heritage 'belongs primarily to that State'. In Decision 44 COM 7A.34 the Committee recalls Article 6.1 of the Convention (heritage as a duty of the international community as a whole) and regrets that the State Party had not fulfilled its obligations under the Convention. Only Articles 4, 6 and 11 were checked; whether the Convention or the Operational Guidelines set out a deletion procedure was not established, and the Operational Guidelines paragraphs on deletion could not be opened and are not quoted here.
outcome: Decision 44 COM 7A.34 (extended 44th session, 2021) decides to delete 'Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City (United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland)' from the World Heritage List. Before that operative paragraph the Committee: expresses serious concern at the Liverpool Waters development under the approved outline planning consent; regrets 'inadequate governance processes, mechanisms, and regulations for new developments' and the resulting serious and irreversible loss of attributes conveying the Outstanding Universal Value; regrets that its earlier appeals did not protect the property; says the approved football stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock adds to the threat; and records that the State Party itself indicated no legal and other means are available in the governance of the property to comply with all the Committee's requests. UNESCO's State of Conservation page records Decision 44 COM 8C.4 as removing the property from the Danger List and deleting it from the World Heritage List. Vote: the Committee's decision pages and UNESCO's news release mention no vote. Boston Globe and Al Jazeera report a secret ballot; Ahram Online alone (in a report that it attributes to AFP) reports 13 in favour and 5 against; this count is single-source and unofficial. No official tally was found.
interpretation: Positions as reported or published by the parties, each attributed. (1) UK Government: an unnamed British government spokesperson was reported by the Boston Globe as expressing disappointment and saying the government still believed that Liverpool deserved World Heritage status 'given the significant role the historic docks and the wider city have played throughout history' (src_06; only the phrase after 'given' is a direct quotation there); Ahram Online (AFP) reports the government said it was 'extremely disappointed' and that Liverpool 'still deserves its world heritage status', the speaker again unnamed (src_08). No gov.uk statement was found. (2) Liverpool City Council: Mayor Joanne Anderson's statement of 21 July 2021 said 'I'm hugely disappointed and concerned by this decision to delete Liverpool's World Heritage status' and 'I find it incomprehensible that UNESCO would rather Bramley Moore Dock remain a derelict wasteland' (src_09); Al Jazeera also quotes her calling the decision 'incomprehensible' (src_07). (3) Steve Rotheram, mayor of the Liverpool City Region (not the City Council or the UK Government), called it 'a retrograde step that does not reflect the reality of what is happening on the ground' (src_07). (4) In its 2021 State of Conservation material the State Party argued that no individual project 'has impacted adversely to a significant extent on the OUV of the property' and that a moratorium on new buildings was 'neither desirable nor practical' (src_02). (5) ICOMOS advised that the stadium proposal 'would have a completely unacceptable major adverse impact on the authenticity and integrity' of the property (src_02).
start_date_display: 2012 (inscription on the List of World Heritage in Danger; day not stated on the decision page)

timeline.title: Liverpool inscribed on the World Heritage List
timeline.description: UNESCO's 2021 news release states the property was inscribed in 2004. (The 2004 inscription decision itself was not read for this entry.)

timeline.title: Committee inscribes the property on the List of World Heritage in Danger (36 COM 7B.93)
timeline.description: The Committee noted that Liverpool City Council was inclined to approve the developer's application for the Liverpool Waters development, expressed serious concern about the potential threat to the property's Outstanding Universal Value, considered the development a potential danger and decided to inscribe the property on the Danger List. The decision stated that the property could be deleted from the World Heritage List if the current project was approved and implemented. It asked for a desired state of conservation for removal from the Danger List and a report by 1 February 2013.

timeline.title: Outline Planning Consent for Liverpool Waters
timeline.description: Decision 43 COM 7A.47 refers to the 'Outline Planning Consent' for Liverpool Waters covering 2013-2042 and describes the resulting developments as an ascertained threat. The exact date of the consent was not read from a planning record.

timeline.title: Committee retains the Danger listing and warns of possible deletion (43 COM 7A.47)
timeline.description: The Committee reiterated serious concern about the Liverpool Waters developments, expressed extreme concern that no moratorium on new buildings had been adopted, and found that recent planning permissions and the State Party's stated inability to control development reflected inadequate governance and planning mechanisms. It kept the property on the Danger List and stated that it would consider deleting it from the World Heritage List at its 44th session if the requirements on a desired state of conservation and a moratorium were not met.

timeline.title: Everton stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock approved
timeline.description: UNESCO's 2021 State of Conservation page records that a full planning application was submitted in December 2019, that the State Party notified the Secretariat in February 2020, that Liverpool City Council approved the project in February 2021, and that media reports indicated approval by the UK Secretary of State in March 2021. It quotes ICOMOS advice that the proposal 'would have a completely unacceptable major adverse impact on the authenticity and integrity' of the property.

timeline.title: Extended 44th session adopts Decision 44 COM 7A.34 and deletes the property
timeline.description: The Committee, at its extended 44th session (Fuzhou and online, per UNESCO's news release), decided to delete 'Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City' from the World Heritage List. The decision regrets, among other points, 'inadequate governance processes, mechanisms, and regulations for new developments' leading to serious and irreversible loss of attributes conveying the Outstanding Universal Value, that the approved stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock adds to the threat, and that the State Party has indicated that no legal and other means are available in the governance of the property to comply with all the Committee's requests. Decision 44 COM 8C.4 ('Update of the List of World Heritage in Danger') is recorded on UNESCO's State of Conservation page as removing the property from the Danger List and deleting it from the World Heritage List.

timeline.title: Vote as reported by media; British government and city reactions
timeline.description: Boston Globe and Al Jazeera report a secret ballot; Ahram Online (AFP copy) alone reports 13 votes in favour and 5 against, which is an unofficial, single-source count. UNESCO's decision page, news release and State of Conservation page do not mention a vote. An unnamed British government spokesperson was reported as expressing disappointment (Boston Globe) and 'extremely disappointed' (Ahram Online). Liverpool Mayor Joanne Anderson issued a statement the same day.

Read through a summarising fetch tool, so only short phrases are quoted verbatim.

sources.title: World Heritage Committee deletes Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City from UNESCO's World Heritage List
sources.reliability_note: UNESCO news release dated 21 July 2021; a communication, not the decision text. Gives the date, the session (44th, Fuzhou and online) and the count of deleted properties. It mentions no vote. It contains one unattributed-in-text sentence ('Any deletion from the World Heritage List is a loss to the international community'), which this dossier does not use.

sources.title: State of Conservation 2021: Liverpool – Maritime Mercantile City
sources.reliability_note: Page for the 2021 session lists the draft decision 44 COM 7A.34 (text matching the adopted version), the stadium chronology, ICOMOS advice, State Party statements and the entry for decision 44 COM 8C.4. It mentions no vote or ballot.

sources.reliability_note: Official decision text, 36th session (2012), working document WHC-12/36.COM/7B.Add. Page gives the year only.

sources.title: Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (text of the Convention)
sources.reliability_note: Official text of the 1972 World Heritage Convention; Articles 4, 6 and 11 were read. The Operational Guidelines' paragraphs on deletion were NOT read (the document could not be opened), so none is cited.

sources.title: Liverpool loses its UNESCO World Heritage status
sources.reliability_note: News report (URL dated 21 July 2021; page metadata gives 22 July 2021). Says the Committee held a secret ballot in Fuzhou, China; gives no vote count. Paraphrases an unnamed British government spokesperson (disappointment; Liverpool still deserved status), with only the phrase 'given the significant role the historic docks and the wider city have played throughout history' directly quoted. Single outlet for these details here; read through a summarising fetch tool.
sources.published_date_display: 21 July 2021 per URL; 22 July 2021 per page metadata

sources.title: UNESCO strips Liverpool of world heritage status
sources.reliability_note: Dated news report. Says the Committee voted by secret ballot; gives no vote count and reports no UK government reaction. Quotes Mayor Joanne Anderson and Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram.

sources.title: UNESCO removes Liverpool waterfront from world heritage list, UK government 'extremely disappointed' at the ruling
sources.reliability_note: Report republished by an Egyptian outlet; the page names the agency as AFP and gives Wednesday 21 July 2021. The ONLY source read that gives a vote count (13 in favour, 5 against, stated to be one more than the two-thirds majority needed); it does not say whether the ballot was secret. The UK government speaker is unnamed. Treat the count as reported, not official.

sources.title: Statement on UNESCO World Heritage Site deletion (Mayor Joanne Anderson, Liverpool City Council)
sources.reliability_note: Council statement by Mayor Joanne Anderson, dated 21 July 2021, republished on a local news site (byline Paul Johnston); the original Liverpool City Council release was not retrieved. Represents the city's own position.

country_links.role: State Party to the Convention; the property was located in Liverpool, England

approval_note: Approved by Harry Disley in chat on 2026-10-15 after reviewing the casebook batch summary; independent verifier checked against official sources. Quotations were read through a summarising fetch tool and should be compared with the original documents before being cited.

changelog.change: Initial draft. Premise checked and confirmed (decision 44 COM 7A.34, 21 July 2021, extended 44th session; Danger List inscription 2012 under 36 COM 7B.93). Known gaps: (1) whc.unesco.org could not be fetched directly (proxy 403); pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, so only short phrases are quoted verbatim and the full decision wording was not independently re-read; (2) the decision pages give the year only; 21 July 2021 comes from UNESCO's news release; (3) the Operational Guidelines paragraphs on deletion could not be opened (permission not granted), so none is cited; Convention Articles 4, 6 and 11 were read; (4) no official vote tally found: the 13-5 count rests on one secondary source (Ahram Online, undated, agency unnamed); secret ballot per Boston Globe and Al Jazeera; the Committee's session report and Rule of Procedure basis for the ballot were not read; (5) UK Government reaction rests on unnamed spokespersons in press reports, no gov.uk statement found; Liverpool City Council statement read via a republication, original release not retrieved; (6) the text of 44 COM 8C.4 was not opened, only its entry on the State of Conservation page; (7) the 2004 inscription decision and the date of the Outline Planning Consent were not read from primary records; (8) stadium approval dates are from UNESCO's State of Conservation page, not planning records. The existing dossier draft-liverpool-maritime-mercantile-city.json was used only to locate URLs; every cited source was opened afresh.

Independent verification against fetched sources. Confirmed: decision 44 COM 7A.34 reference and operative text; 21 July 2021 and Fuzhou/online session (UNESCO news release 2314); 2004 inscription, 2012 Danger listing, third deletion; 44 COM 8C.4 wording; 36 COM 7B.93 and 43 COM 7A.47 content (incl. paragraph on inadequate governance); stadium chronology and ICOMOS/State Party quotes; Convention Arts 4, 6, 11(4) quotes; Anderson and Rotheram quotes. Fixes: (1) 'let down' for the UK government spokesperson was not in the Boston Globe; replaced with 'disappointment' paraphrase, noting only one phrase is a direct quote (timeline, interpretation, src_06 note); (2) vote count now explicitly attributed as single-source, via Ahram Online which names AFP, and unofficial; src_08 note updated (agency AFP, date 21 July 2021); (3) Boston Globe date discrepancy (URL 21 July, metadata 22 July) recorded; (4) legal_basis: removed 'read through a summarising tool' phrasing and replaced with exact Article 11(4) phrases; (5) src_01 note wrongly said no quotations; corrected; (6) outcome 'appeals from 2012 to 2019' softened to 'earlier appeals' per decision wording; (7) src_09 byline noted. Not independently verified: official vote tally or Rule of Procedure for the secret ballot; Operational Guidelines deletion paragraphs; original Council release; 2004 inscription decision; planning-record dates; fetches were via a summarising tool so exact full wording of decisions was not re-read.
Approved by Harry Disley; copied to approved/ for import.
